newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Beximco targets foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Beximco targets foreign markets.

text.p: Beximco Pharmaceuticals is one of the few Bangladesh companies to make inroads into a difficult and competitive international drug market.
"We are now aiming to have a share of the U.S. and European markets," Salman F. Rahman, vice-chairman of the company, told Reuters.
The company is acquiring technology to produce drugs of U.S. standard, he said.
"India and Russia are our main competitors in Europe. We are marketing in a highly competitive environment. At least 30 companies are offering the same products under different names."

Beximco's finished products and chemicals are exported to Malaysia, Thailand, South Korea, Russia and Taiwan, and the firm will starting exporting to Vietnam this year. The company will export $13 million worth of medicines and raw materials to Vietnam, company officials said. "This is a major breakthrough in our efforts for greater exposure," one official said.
The value of export volumes may rise to $20 million in 1996, which is a 100 percent increase from the previous year, they said.

Beximco Pharmaceuticals was a "permanent blue chip and I don't see any hurdles for its growth at home and abroad. The breakthrough by the Beximco in overseas markets is a great achievement for a country like Bangladesh," Syed Mamun Mahbub, Chairman of Jasmine Securities Ltd, said.

"The excellent professional management is the crux of the company's success over past several years. We encourage taking decisions at operational levels," said Abdul Mukhtadir, executive director of the company.

He said Beximco Pharmaceuticals Ltd (BPL), a listed company with a domestic market share of 15 percent, faces competition from 10 other companies in the country, including Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Inc and Fisons Plc, and local firms Square Pharmaceuticals and ACI Ltd..

BPL's product line includes 78 formulation products covering all major therapeutic classes and two widely used antibiotic raw materials -- Ampicillin Trihydrates and Amoxycillin Trihydrates. The company supplies 90 percent of the domestic needs for these two raw materials.
"BPL is the only local company producing these raw materials, thus giving it a slight advantage in terms of cost," Peregrine Capital Ltd, a Hong Kong-based fund manager, said in an analysis of BPL.
It said Beximco Pharmaceuticals should continue to grow with the help of its "highly professional management team, quality products, vertical integration and a well-developed distribution network".
Rahman said BPL had made a $20 million investment in a new plant conforming to standards set by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
"Once the plant is completed and certified by the USFDA, the company aims to enter the United States pharmaceutical market. This will dramatically increase the company's growth and profit," he said.
He said Pharmagen Beximco, a BPL subsidiary in Pakistan, was meeting almost 100 percent of that country's requirement for Ampicillin and Amoxycillin Trihydrates.
Rahman said BPL was planning to set up a similar company in Vietnam.
Beximco officials said BPL's net after-tax profit rose by about 10 percent to 310.2 million taka ($7.4 million) in the year ended December 31, 1995.
Sales turnover was 2.02 billion taka in the 1995 calendar year against 1.65 billion taka in the previous year.
The 10-taka Beximco Pharmaceuticals share was traded on the Dhaka Stock Exchange at 235.31 taka on Wednesday.
